ISO 3901:2019 Standard • US ISRC Agency Registrant #185611

Official US ISRC Registrant Prefix: QTAHP & ERR Catalog Registry

On October 20, 2026, the official United States ISRC Agency allocated the permanent Registrant Code AHP (Country + Registrant Prefix: QTAHP) to Michael Ragsdale (Engine Room Records). Every sound recording minted under the QTAHP prefix is 100% independently produced, mastered, and owned by Michael P. Ragsdale.

2. Real-World Administration vs. In-Universe World-Building

Real-World Engine Room Records vs. Fictional Engine Room Records, LLC — And How ERR Catalog Numbers Bridge Both

Because our projects weave concept albums into interconnected novels and archival lore, we maintain a strict, transparent boundary between our real-world legal administration and our fictional narrative universe—while using a unified ERR Catalog Numbering System across both.

Real-World Layer (Non-Fiction)

Engine Room Records (Michael P. Ragsdale)

In the real world, there is only Engine Room Records (never with “LLC”). It is the real-world creative brand and publishing imprint of sole human creator Michael P. Ragsdale.

All real-world identifiers—including US ISRC Agency Prefix QTAHP (Registrant #185611), GS1/distributor UPC barcodes, and our sole authorized distributor account on DistroKid—belong strictly to Michael P. Ragsdale.

In-Universe Layer (100% Fiction)

Engine Room Records, LLC (Holly O’Connell)

Anything with LLC, Trust, or Holdings in its name (including Engine Room Records, LLC, The O’Connell Family, LLC, Artists First Management, LLC, and Stardust Properties, LLC) is strictly a fictitious, in-universe narrative entity.

In our stories, Engine Room Records, LLC was founded in 1992 by the fictional character Holly O’Connell to rescue The Stardust Engine’s master tapes from the fictional conglomerate Apex Records. (Explore the Corporate Lore →)

Shared Dual-Layer Bridge

ERR Catalog Numbers (ERR-001-2015-101)

Unlike QTAHP (which is strictly real-world), our ERR Catalog Numbers are real to Michael P. Ragsdale and used interchangeably in-universe by Holly O’Connell!

In the real world, our studio build script (Harper) mints an ERR-ID for every track in master-catalog.json and embeds it in ID3v2/RIFF metadata. In-universe, that exact same ERR-ID is the archival vault number stamped on Holly O’Connell’s master tape reels in Blacksburg, VA.

How to Read an ERR Catalog Number (e.g., ERR-001-2015-101)

Every track in the Engine Room Records catalog is indexed by a four-part hyphenated key (ERR-<RosterCode>-<EraYear>-<DiscTrack>) shared between Michael P. Ragsdale’s real-world master ledger and Holly O’Connell’s in-universe vault:

1. Imprint & Artist Roster Prefix (ERR-001 – ERR-008):
  • ERR-001 — The Stardust Engine (Rock Opera / Progressive Synth-Rock)
  • ERR-002 — Fractured Prisms (Industrial / Melodic Post-Hardcore)
  • ERR-003 — The Paper Wall (Alternative / Indie Rock)
  • ERR-004 — Firelight (Acoustic / Heartland Folk-Rock)
  • ERR-005 — The Arctic Symphony Project (Cinematic Symphonic Metal)
  • ERR-006 — Crimson Node (Cyberpunk Synthwave / Darksynth)
  • ERR-007 — Mana Canvas (Runebreaker Fantasy Orchestral / Chiptune)
  • ERR-008 — The Hoshizora Ensemble (1970s Japanese City Pop / Jazz Fusion)
2. Era Year & Disc/Track Index (-2015-101):
  • Middle 4 Digits (2015): The album’s canonical era or release year (for example, 1987 for Electric Color, 2001 for Midnight Drivers, or 2015 for Reignition).
  • Final 3 Digits (101): The disc number (1 = Disc 1) followed by the two-digit track number (01 = Track 1; e.g., Disc 3 Track 8 of Live at the Crucible is 308).
  • Try It Above: Paste any ERR-... number into the Interactive Decoder above to resolve its corresponding QTAHP or QZ... ISRC!
3. ISO 3901:2019 Technical Structure

How to Read an Engine Room Records QTAHP ISRC

Every 12-character International Standard Recording Code (ISRC) issued by Engine Room Records follows the strict four-segment ISO 3901:2019 specification. Here is how Track 1 of The Stardust Engine — Reignition (QTAHP2600046) breaks down:

QTAHP2600046
Example Recording: “Reignition: Lights Up on Progress Street” — The Stardust Engine (Catalog ID: ERR-001-2015-101)
Characters 1–2 • Country Code

QT — United States (US ISRC Agency)

Because the United States music industry exhausted the original US, QM, and QZ two-character country namespaces, the International ISRC Registration Authority (IFPI) allocated QT exclusively to the United States ISRC Agency. Any ISRC beginning with QT originates from a registered United States rights holder.

Characters 3–5 • Registrant Code

AHP — Michael Ragsdale / Engine Room Records

Permanently assigned to Michael Ragsdale (Registrant #185611). Unlike distributor-suballocated codes where the 3-character registrant block belongs to the aggregator, AHP identifies Michael P. Ragsdale / Engine Room Records directly in the global DDEX supply chain across Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, and SoundExchange.

Characters 6–7 • Year of Reference

26 — Real-World Allocation Year (2026)

Per ISO 3901:2019 §4.3, these two digits represent the real-world calendar year in which the ISRC is allocated to the recording (26 = 2026). Under our Dual Timelines Policy, even when a concept album is set in an earlier in-universe narrative era (such as 1978, 1987, or 2015), the ISRC Year of Reference and DSP release year always reflect the true real-world production year.

Characters 8–12 • Designation Code

00046 — Sequential Master Designation

A unique, monotonically increasing 5-digit integer (starting at 00001 each calendar year) assigned automatically by our studio build engineer, Harper (harper.sh), the moment a final 48kHz/16-bit stereo PCM WAV master is locked into the local studio vault.

4. Governance & Chain of Custody

The Permanent Single-ISRC Rule & Why You Will See Both QTAHP and QZ... Codes

Rule 1: Never Re-Mint an Existing Recording’s ISRC

Under ISO 3901:2019, a sound recording may only ever have one ISRC for its entire lifespan, and an ISRC may never be reused for a different recording. All Engine Room Records releases published prior to October 20, 2026 received valid ISRCs from DistroKid’s sub-allocated US ISRC blocks (beginning with QZW..., QZR..., or QTA7V...). Those 255 recordings permanently keep their original ISRCs forever.

Similarly, when an identical master recording appears on both a primary album and a companion archival release (such as “Ignition: The Forger’s Call [Live at the Crucible]”, QTAHP2600043), both releases reference the exact same ISRC so play counts and rights metadata remain unified.

Rule 2: Binary Embedding Across All Audio Tiers

Whenever Harper (harper.sh) processes a master WAV in the studio vault, the track’s canonical ISRC (whether QTAHP26xxxxx or legacy QZ...) and ERR Catalog Number are written directly into the binary container headers of every distribution tier:

  • 48kHz / 16-bit Lossless WAV (vault/wav/): Embedded in the RIFF LIST/INFO ISRC chunk and Broadcast Wave (bext) header.
  • Lossless FLAC & Ogg Vorbis (vault/flac/, vault/ogg/): Embedded as standard Vorbis ISRC and CATALOGNUMBER comments.
  • MP3 320kbps V0 & 128kbps Web Stream (web-mp3/): Embedded in ID3v2.3 TSRC frames alongside full AI & CC BY-SA 4.0 disclosures.
